meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate registry distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code heritage, harmonized with EU law and supplemented by Luxembourg commercial statutes)

Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU, as amended (EU-wide dividend relief framework)
Interest and Royalties Directive 2003/49/EC, as amended
EU-Singapore Investment Protection Agreement (in force; EU investment protection framework)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution in the country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, managers, and legal representatives against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions regimes, OFAC SDN list, and Luxembourg FIU (CRF) guidance. PEPs, their family members, and close associates require enhanced due diligence under Articles 2-3 of the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, including source-of-wealth verification and STR filing obligations to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the primary administrative language of the RCS. Company names must be rendered in Latin script; non-Latin names require approved transliteration. The legal form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' is mandatory. The name must be distinctive, not confusingly similar to an existing registered name, not misleading about the company's legal form or activity, and must not violate public order or morality.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Société / Holding / SARL when used in a manner that misrepresents legal form
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, file a new pre-reservation application with additional distinguishing elements or challenge the refusal before the President of the Luxembourg City Tribunal d'arrondissement in summary proceedings (référé) within 15 days of the written refusal, attaching the RCS decision and proposed corporate name documentation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the statutory registered office (siège social). Luxembourg requires a genuine physical establishment with operational substance; virtual-office-only arrangements are rejected by the RCS and may lead to deregistration or sanctions under the Companies Law of 10 August 1915.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25 percent probability of unannounced on-site inspection for a manufacturing/handling site under product-safety, customs, and social-security audit plans; approximately 5 percent for a pure administrative office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 179 to 200 (SARL provisions), as amended by the Law of 23 September 2016; supplemented by the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Ministry of Justice; exclusive e-filing channel: MyGuichet.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif) with Articles of Association (Statuts), filed at the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum share capital under Article 179 of the Law of 10 August 1915. The capital must be fully subscribed; at least 25% of each cash share (minimum EUR 3,000) must be paid into a blocked escrow account (compte de souscription bloqué) at a Luxembourg credit institution before RCS registration. In-kind contributions are fully paid up at incorporation and require a réviseur d'entreprises statutory auditor's report. The remaining 75% is payable within five years.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] S.À R.L.
Adopted on [date] by the sole shareholder.
RESOLVED:
1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION: The share capital of EUR 12,000 is fully subscribed and EUR 3,000, representing 25%, has been paid into a blocked escrow account at [Bank].
2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office is fixed at [Address], Luxembourg.
3. OFFICER APPOINTMENT: [Name] is appointed as sole manager (gérant), with sole signature power, and is authorized to register the Company with the RCS, to obtain the VAT number and settle all incorporation formalities.
Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS Luxembourg / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation request on MyGuichet.lu for the proposed name(s). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names and must include the legal form suffix 'S.à r.l.' The granted certificate of availability must be attached to the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation form (Formulaire de réservation du nom)
Passport copies of proposed shareholders and managers
Copy of draft Articles of Association with proposed name and corporate purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, file a new reservation with revised name variants; if the RCS query is based on screening doubts, request a written justification from LBR and submit corrected name variants within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Blocked Subscription Capital Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État / Spuerkeess)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account (compte de souscription bloqué) in the name of the company in formation with a Luxembourg-established bank. Deposit at least EUR 3,000 representing 25% of the minimum capital. The bank issues a blocking attestation (attestation de blocage des fonds) which is released to the company upon RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association / incorporation project
Company name availability certificate from RCS
Passport and proof of address of each subscriber/shareholder
Bank KYC and AML questionnaires
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC evidence, provide notarized or apostilled documents; if the bank refuses the account under its onboarding policies, transfer the application to another licensed Luxembourg credit institution and re-deposit the funds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Signing of the Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire luxembourgeois) or private writing under the signatures of all shareholders (acte sous seing privé)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the Articles of Association (acte constitutif/statuts). For a SARL with cash contributions, a private deed signed by all shareholders is admissible; if in-kind contributions are made, a réviseur d'entreprises valuation report is mandatory. Appoint the manager(s) and deliver the statutory declarations confirming no bankruptcy and no criminal convictions.
required_dossiers: Final Articles of Association
Bank capital blocking attestation
Statutory auditor's report on in-kind contributions (if applicable)
Manager appointment consents and statutory declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or governing authorities detect inconsistencies, amend the deed by a corrective notarial rider or re-execute the private deed with the signatures of all shareholders; if using the private deed, correct and re-sign before all shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration Filing and Legal Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS Luxembourg (Luxembourg Business Registers) - electronic filing on MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed deed and the standard registration form through MyGuichet.lu, attach the bank blocking certificate and manager declarations, and pay the registration fee (approx. EUR 75). The RCS verifies the deed against mandatory legal provisions, allocates the RCS number, and records the company.
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation deed
RCS standard registration form
Bank attestation of paid-up capital
Manager consents and declarations of honor
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (demande de complément), respond within 15 calendar days with the requested rectification; upon rejection, appeal to the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within the statutory delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in RESA and Post-Filing Administrative Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once registered, the RCS posts the legal notice in RESA, giving the incorporation legal validity against third parties. Thereafter, apply for the Luxembourg VAT number at the AEDT, register with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) as an employer, and obtain the EORI/CAD number and the autorisation d'établissement from the Ministry of the Economy.
required_dossiers: RCS incorporation extract
Residential/address proof for the registered office
VAT application forms
Autorisation d'établissement application file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed, contact LBR to expedite the posting; if VAT registration is queried, complete the AEDT file with the RCS extract and supporting evidence; any rejected application may be re-submitted through the guichet.lu mediation channel.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Directorate General for Industry (Direction générale de l'industrie); single point of contact: Guichet unique (guichet.lu)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Establishment Authorization (Autorisation d'établissement) issued under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the craft, commercial and industrial professions

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified establishment (établissement classé) under the amended Law of 10 June 1999; a polyresin vacuum casting and hand-painting workshop of this scope is typically a Class 3 declaration, upgraded to a Class 2 operating authorization where installed capacity exceeds regulatory thresholds; a full EIA applies only at the Annex II thresholds of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 July 2019 and the European Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive; VOC/solvent emissions must remain below the 5 tonnes per year threshold of Annex VII of Directive 2010/75/EU; waste, including resin and catalyst residues, must be managed under the amended Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management and delivered to authorized recovery or disposal facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) verifying means of escape, extinguishers, and safe storage of flammable resins; structural load inspection certificate for the workshop floor; and workplace safety clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), based on the risk assessment (document unique), ventilation control, PPE provision and first-aid organization.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; official filing and registration portals: impotsdirects.public.lu, myguichet.lu, and the Tax-on-Web e-filing platform for Luxembourg VAT and subscription tax declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign owner of a Luxembourg SARL must (1) enrol the company at the Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) through an appointed local manager by filing the articles of association and the registered office declaration, thereby obtaining the business registration number that serves as the master corporate identifier; (2) obtain the 13-digit national identification number (NIF) from the ACD once the registration is published; (3) file the VAT registration form (Form 640) with the AEDT to secure the LU+8-digit VAT identification number before making any taxable supply in Luxembourg; and (4) complete ancillary registrations (CCSS social security for staff, beneficial ownership declaration at the LBR, and EORI application with the Luxembourg customs administration for export operations). VAT registration is mandatory without turnover threshold where a taxable transaction occurs, but small undertakings may claim the EUR 35,000 annual turnover exemption for supplies to non-taxable persons; the EUR 10,000 threshold applies to intra-Community distance sales and OSS services. A non-resident manager or day-to-day director requires an EU/EEA/Swiss residence address to preserve the Luxembourg management seat.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (worldwide taxation of a resident SARL; territorial exemptions available under the participation-exemption regime); a SARL is a fully taxable resident company if its registered office or central administration is in Luxembourg, and is subject to corporate income tax (statutory rate 17% for income above the EUR 175,000 band; approximate aggregate effective rate of 24.94% in Luxembourg City including the solidarity/unemployment surcharge and communal business tax), net wealth tax (0.5% annual), and full VAT liability. There is no pass-through or check-the-box regime for SARLs, no tax-exempt zone regime for manufacturing, and non-resident ownership of capital is fully permitted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no U.S.-style check-the-box election in Luxembourg, but the SARL may elect: (i) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR for intra-group resident losses and profit offsets; (ii) participation exemption (Schachtelprivileg) election to exempt qualifying dividends and capital gains; (iii) notional interest deduction (NID) on qualifying new equity; (iv) IP Box deduction for qualifying intellectual property income; (v) group VAT unit as a single taxable person for financial/insurance groups under Article 60(3) of the VAT law; and (vi) express election to leave the small-undertaking scheme by registering for VAT even below the threshold. ATAD hybrid mismatch provisions (Article 168bis LIR) operate as mandatory disallowances and cannot be contracted around by election or hybrid instruments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA) as codified by the VAT Law of 12 February 1979 implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by the AEDT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover for supplies to final consumers (small-undertaking exemption, electable); EUR 10,000 annual turnover for intra-Community distance sales and electronic/telecom services (OSS threshold); no threshold for physical B2B supplies in Luxembourg subject to the obligation of self-identification and reverse charge by the customer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time clearance, tax-authority stamping, or continuous transaction-control API applies to B2B/B2C invoicing in Luxembourg. Mandatory e-invoicing applies to B2G contracts with central public entities since 1 January 2024 and will be extended to all public-sector purchasers through 2026; invoices must comply with EN 16931 and be transmitted through the national Peppol network (Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 with UBL or Factur-X); suppliers must expose a Peppol access point (API connectivity) but no fiscal pre-clearance exists. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary in PDF/XML; EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) will introduce transaction-based e-invoicing and digital reporting for intra-Community supplies on a projected 2030/2035 timeline.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating applies when the SARL dispatches polyresin statues and garage kits outside the EU for a consideration and can prove that the goods physically left EU customs territory within 90 days from the supply (rebuttable presumption per EU Implementing Regulation 2018/1912 and AEDT practice). Eligibility requires a valid electronic export declaration (SAD) accepted by the customs office of actual export, reliable transport evidence (CMR/airway bill/bill of lading), the commercial invoice, and a corresponding EORI-linked shipment record. Plastic statuettes and composite resin articles under HS 3926 (e.g., 3926.40) require correct CN classification; artistic/replica statues may fall under HS 9705/4420 where applicable. Directly related export services may also be zero-rated. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is refundable through monthly/quarterly Tax-on-Web claims; non-established EU suppliers use the EU VAT refund procedure (Directive 2008/9/EC) and non-EU suppliers use the Thirteenth Directive regime, with proof of export held in the refund file.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic SAD with validated EORI number in Luxembourg customs IT system)
Transport documentation proving cross-border exit: CMR waybill for road transport, bill of lading for sea freight, or air waybill for air cargo
Commercial invoice issued by LU_SARL with reference to the export declaration
Customs exit confirmation (electronic 'exitus' message in the EU NCTS) or customs stamp for non-NCTS consignments
Inward remittance certificate / bank statement evidencing settlement by the non-EU buyer
Warehouse exit register or sworn carrier attestation for consignment and hub-export flows
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT law does not impose a statutory FX-repatriation condition inside the zero-rating rule; the 180-day figure is the compliance pipeline standard for receipt of export funds. The AEDT applies heightened audit scrutiny to export zero-rating when goods are declared through the SARL rather than by the customer and when documentation is digital-only; absence of 90-day export proof causes retrospective re-characterisation as a domestic taxable supply, generating VAT at 17%, late-payment interest at 0.8% per commenced month, and administrative fines (statutory fine bands, multiplied up to 3 times the evaded VAT in proven fraud cases). Deliberate sham-export schemes attract criminal prosecution before the Luxembourg criminal courts, extension of the statute of limitation from 3 to 10 years, revocation of EORI and customs simplifications, denial of input VAT deduction, publication of sanction decisions, and, for group structures, joint and several liability of the SARL's legal representatives.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — monetary authority, balance-of-payments statistics, and FX-market supervision; Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) — competent authority for credit institutions, payment institutions, and AML/CFT supervision; Ministère des Finances — EU/UN financial sanctions enforcement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Resident currency is the euro (EUR); full convertibility on both current and capital account under Articles 63–66 TFEU and the EU Capital Movements Directive (88/361/EEC). No Luxembourg exchange control law, no prior authorization, no forex declaration, and no mandatory EUR conversion applies to inbound equity injections, export receivables, or profit remittances. Dividend distributions to a foreign parent are unrestricted under the Law of 10 August 1915 solvency tests and incur 15% withholding tax, reducible to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (10% participation held ≥12 months); no exchange-control surcharge applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg does not impose any statutory timeline, surrender ratio, or repatriation obligation for export proceeds in EUR or foreign currency. Export revenues from resin-statue e-commerce (Stripe/PayPal USD/EUR settlements) may be retained freely, converted at market EUR/USD rates, or used directly to pay foreign suppliers; only statistical BCL balance-of-payments reporting via bank purpose codes (e.g., S001/S109) is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital blocked account (compte bloqué) for the €12,000 SARL statutory minimum capital; operational current account in EUR
Operational account (EUR and USD); trade finance / commercial LC; FX hedging line
Operational account (EUR), treasury and cash management, e-commerce merchant settlement
Operational account (EUR/USD) and cash-pooling for holding structures
Operational account (EUR) for EU re-invoicing and Italian supplier corridors
Operational account (EUR) with private-banking service layer

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH as a supplementary collection and FX conversion rail, but not as the primary corporate bank. EU-licensed EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) can passport into Luxembourg under PSD2 and are CSSF-supervised, and they may lawfully safeguard e-commerce proceeds in segregated accounts at EU credit institutions; however, an EMI cannot hold the SARL statutory capital blocked account (Art. 710-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915 requires a Luxembourg credit institution), cannot issue or confirm commercial letters of credit, and is not eligible for the RCS/notarial capital certificate. Recommended structure: Tier-1 bank for capital/escrow, LC and settlement; a CSSF-registered EMI for high-frequency Stripe/PayPal USD collection sweeps and sub-€50k supplier disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible under the Law of 12 November 2004 (AML/CFT) and CSSF Regulation 12-02 when the bank uses eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures and a compliant video-KYC solution, but prevailing Tier-1 market practice (BCEE, BGL, BIL) still requires at least one physical UBO/director interview at the Luxembourg branch, or a sworn attestation before a Luxembourg notary, for a 100% foreign-owned SARL. Plan for one physical visit by the UBO to Luxembourg; a local registered agent may handle administrative filings (RBE declaration, RESA publication) under power of attorney, but account signature cards and UBO identification must be executed personally or via QES if the bank so permits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO / 100% foreign ownership — bank demands clarity on the final beneficial owner and the origin of the €12,000 share capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE registration certificate; certified passport copies of UBO and directors; 12-month shareholder bank statements evidencing legitimate savings; corporate charter, certificate of incumbency and apostilled power of attorney from the home jurisdiction; sworn CV and professional references for the UBO; breakdown of capital funds (own funds, no third-party loans).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face e-commerce model — fragmented pre-order deposits via Stripe and PayPal trigger heightened transaction-monitoring expectations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Domain/brand registration and IP certificates; Stripe/PayPal platform agreements and 6-month settlement statements projected to Luxembourg; product catalog and pricing list for ISIC 3240/NAICS 339930 statues; chargeback/refund policy; warehouse/fulfillment contracts; sample commercial invoices and shipping records (DHL/UPS/FedEx) tying each collection to physical delivery.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value collectibles interface — resin statues may be perceived as vehicles for value transfer or cross-border payment masking
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg VAT registration and distance-selling compliance evidence; copyright/design registrations for each statue edition; serialized edition-numbering and certificate-of-authenticity templates; export/import licenses (none required for polyresin toys, but customs classification TARIC 9503.00.75 documentation); documented refusal log for suspicious purchasers and sanctions-scanned customer records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border supplier payments to non-EEA countries (e.g., resin raw materials, pigments from China) — mismatch between small company size and large trade-route volumes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase contracts; pro-forma invoices and Bills of Lading; import customs declarations (Luxembourg customs broker records); quality inspection certificates; bank purpose-code narrative matching the SWIFT MT103 remittance; annual business plan with inventory turnover projections consistent with pre-order sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP screening — US retail customer base and possible high-net-worth collectors create screening noise
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions/PEP screening tool outputs (e.g., LexisNexis Bridger, Dow Jones); negative-hit false-positive resolution file; written client-acceptance policy for low-risk standard e-commerce; compliance manual incorporating CSSF Circular 20/744 on asset freezes; refusal-and-refund register; escalation procedure to the CSSF/FIU for any reportable incident.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder equity is wired in EUR via SWIFT MT103 to the SARL's blocked account at a Luxembourg credit institution before notarization (min. €12,000 under Art. 710-1); BCL balance-of-payments purpose code S001 (Direct investment — equity capital) must be entered in the wire's remittance information; the remitter name must match the shareholder disclosed in the incorporation file to avoid AML rejection; no BCL prior approval is required. After the notarial deed, RESA publication and RCS registration, the bank releases the block and funds move by internal transfer to the operational account. If the foreign shareholder wires USD, conversion to EUR occurs at the remitting bank or via the Luxembourg receiving bank's EUR/USD spot; the blocked-account certificate is then issued by the credit institution for the notary.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR for intra-EEA suppliers (T+1 settlement, no correspondent fees); (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA raw-material purchases with purpose code and documentary backup (invoice, packing list, Bill of Lading); (3) Commercial Letter of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700 under UCP 600 for bulk resin/pigment procurement requiring bank payment undertakings — available through BGL BNP Paribas/BIL trade desks; (4) Stripe/PayPal settlements routed from their EU acquiring banks into the Luxembourg operational account via SEPA or MT103; (5) corporate purchasing card for sub-threshold consumables and freight; USD outflows are converted at spot via the bank or an EMI sweep account; all disbursements must be reconciled against pre-order deposits to maintain audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable vanilla FX forward (OTC) — tenors 1–12 months under ISDA 2002 or a Luxembourg FX Master Agreement, with BGL BNP Paribas or BIL; aligned to pre-order deposit cycle.
EUR/USD FX swap (tom-next/spot-next) — intra-month liquidity rebalancing between USD e-commerce collections and EUR supplier disbursements.
EUR/USD European-style FX option (call/put) — premium-bounded protection for concentrated one-off collections (large limited-edition launches).
EUR/USD zero-cost collar — for a confirmed annual order book; removes premium cost while capping downside/upside.
Cross-currency swap (EUR/USD) — permissible but disfavored for the SARL absent long-term debt; only if a trade-finance facility is structured with the bank.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — not applicable and not offered by Luxembourg resident banks: EUR is fully convertible and a deep onshore deliverable EUR/USD market exists; NDFs would carry prohibitive pricing and regulatory documentation burden.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) approval, filing, and publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting must be held within 6 months of financial year end; for a calendar-year SARL, AGM by 30 June and accounts filed with RCS within 1 month of approval, normally by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a formal RCS notice and judicial injunction; continued default may lead to a periodic penalty payment (astreinte) and, after repeated non-compliance, administrative dissolution and strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 15 March of the following calendar year; any change in beneficial ownership must additionally be filed within one month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missing confirmation exposes the SARL and its managers to administrative fines, publication of non-compliance, and criminal fines under the Luxembourg anti-money laundering register rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and municipal business tax returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, e-filing by 31 May; later deadline only if a valid extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts default interest at 0.6% per month on assessed tax, possible administrative fines, and loss of deductible items or tax credits

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) if it exceeds two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, or 50 average employees
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory annual accounts must be prepared under Luxembourg GAAP (LUX GAAP) pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002, implementing the EU Accounting Directive; IFRS is permitted for consolidated accounts or where specifically required for public-interest entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year, the SARL must verify its RBE data and confirm the current beneficial owners by 15 March. Any transfer of shares or change in ultimate ownership must be reported to the RBE within one month; the annual confirmation serves as the mandatory periodic attestation that the registered data remain accurate.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – 18,000 per year for a small, non-complex SARL

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined headline rate for Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax); other communes apply municipal business tax rates between approximately 6.75% and 11.2%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains on participations of at least 10% or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost held for at least 12 months; sub-threshold portfolio dividends benefit from a 50% exemption; grandfathered IP box (80% exemption) limited to qualifying IP created or acquired before 1 July 2016; notional interest deduction on incremental net equity; no time limit for loss carryforward

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 100 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) covering corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; filed electronically via the MyGuichet.lu e-Filing portal of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year ending 31 December: return due by 30 September of the following year; non-calendar fiscal years: within nine months of the fiscal year-end; written extension requests are granted by the ACD at its discretion

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification: RCS Luxembourg registration number, Luxembourg VAT identification number, NACE 3240 activity code, registered office address, place of central administration and management
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident SARL must declare the RCS number and demonstrate that central administration and decision-making remain in Luxembourg; non-residents with a Luxembourg permanent establishment file the same form and identify the PE address

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period: opening and closing dates of the accounting year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the identical accounting period as the statutory financial statements; short or long first-year periods must be prorated accordingly

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit (bénéfice de l'exercice) per the statutory income statement before tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident SARL reports worldwide income; income allocable to a foreign permanent establishment or deriving from DTA-covered sources must be separately flagged for exemption or credit

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs: non-deductible expenses including fines, tax penalties, excessive director fees, non-deductible entertainment costs, and unjustified management fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Each intra-group expense must be substantiated with contracts, invoices and arm's-length evidence; absence of sub-stantiating documentation triggers automatic add-back

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: participation-exempt dividends and capital gains, grandfathered IP box income, notional interest deduction, unutilized loss carryforwards, and 50% dividends-received exemption for sub-threshold holdings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach participation register, holding-period proof, and loss carryforward schedule; foreign dividends require documentary evidence of the underlying foreign corporate tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax base (impôt commercial communal) after deductibility adjustments and loss offsets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the municipal multiplier of the commune of the registered office; Luxembourg City applies 6.75%, which forms the 24.94% combined headline rate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax base (IRC) and computed tax at 17%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply DTA foreign tax credit or exemption where Luxembourg retains residual taxing rights; attach Form 100 schedules for treaty positions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Solidarity surcharge: 7% of the assessed corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The surcharge applies to resident SARLs and to Luxembourg branches of non-resident companies; refundable investment tax credits may reduce the base

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and prepayments: quarterly prepayments of CIT, foreign tax credits, and withholding tax credits on outbound payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepayments against Luxembourg CIT must be aligned with the estimated tax base; underpayment gives rise to monthly interest charges

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 0.5% monthly late-payment interest (§ 219 Tax Adaptation Law) plus administrative tax increases of 25%–100% on ex officio assessments; failure to maintain or produce books gives rise to fines up to EUR 25,000; deliberate non-filing constitutes tax fraud with criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 per tax year per tax and imprisonment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory withholding tax on dividends; 0% for qualifying distributions under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (minimum 10% shareholding held at least 12 months); 0% for repayments of subscribed share capital
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The paying Luxembourg SARL must collect from the foreign recipient: (i) Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the recipient's tax authority; (ii) signed beneficial ownership declaration; (iii) shareholding and holding-period evidence; upon validation, the reduced treaty rate (typically 5% for corporate shareholders, 15% for individuals) is applied at payment date; if treaty relief cannot be applied at source, the recipient may reclaim excess withholding via an ACD refund application within three years following the distribution

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents: 0% domestic withholding tax (permanently abolished as of 1 January 2007); most Luxembourg DTA networks confirm 0% or limited 5%–10% rates. Interest paid to non-resident corporate creditors: 0% domestic withholding tax; a 20% domestic withholding tax applies only to interest payments made to Luxembourg-resident individuals (effective 1 January 2021), with treaty relief available for foreign individuals

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 group consolidated turnover triggers mandatory Master File and Local File; per-transaction Local File thresholds are EUR 1,000,000 for goods, EUR 500,000 for other services, EUR 250,000 for financial transactions (interest) and intangible royalty flows; Country-by-Country reporting required for groups with consolidated turnover above EUR 750,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate formal Economic Substance Regulations; substance is nevertheless mandated through the abuse-of-law clause (article 6 Tax Adaptation Law), ATAD GAAR and the administrative concept of real activity. A resin-statue SARL must maintain physical premises, local employees, active board decisions in Luxembourg, and genuine commercial activity; a 'letterbox' profile risks refusal of tax residency certificates, denial of DTA benefits, re-qualification of payments as constructive dividends, and ATAD Unshell scrutiny.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of resin-statue online sales collected via Stripe and PayPal, issuance of forged invoices, concealment of inventory, or destruction of accounting records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of all underpaid taxes plus 0.5% monthly late-payment interest; criminal fines of EUR 25,000 to EUR 250,000 per tax year per tax; aggravated fraud using organized or cross-border arrangements increases fines and imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for reassessed corporate taxes and unpaid withholding amounts; criminal conviction triggers imprisonment between five and ten years, travel bans, prohibition from managing commercial companies, and civil restitution of evaded sums

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Letterbox Shell Company / Abuse of Law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining Luxembourg registration solely to access the DTA network while all management, production, staffing and commercial activity occurs abroad; absence of local substance for the resin casting, hand-painting or distribution operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Abuse-of-law reassessment with a 50% increase of the evaded tax; refusal of the ACD tax residence certificate; cancellation of VAT registration; compulsory de-registration from the Luxembourg trade register; administrative bookkeeping fines up to EUR 25,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors' personal assets attachable for reassessed taxes; deemed constructive dividends taxed at 15% withholding; travel restrictions and disqualification from board positions in Luxembourg until full settlement

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and file ultimate beneficial owners in the Luxembourg RBE register; missing AML/KYC documentation for resellers and high-volume Stripe/PayPal collections routed to accounts of unnamed third parties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the AML Law of 12 November 2004 as amended: up to EUR 1,000,000 for the legal entity and up to EUR 250,000 for individuals; persistent breach triggers RBE de-registration, freezing of bank accounts, and compulsory winding-up
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal liability for money laundering and facilitation of undeclared flows (imprisonment up to five years); civil restitution, international travel bans, asset seizure, and permanent disqualification from commercial activity

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Execution of intra-group transactions—resin mixing services, statue design royalties, intercompany loans, or distribution arrangements—at non-arm's-length prices, or omission of the Local File/Master File once the EUR 50 million group revenue threshold is exceeded
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer pricing adjustment plus 0.5% monthly interest; administrative fines up to EUR 250,000; disallowance of deductible intra-group expenses; secondary adjustment treated as constructive dividend exposing a 15% withholding tax obligation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly liable for missing TP documentation and unpaid withholding taxes; participation in artificial pricing triggers criminal aiding of tax evasion; professional ban and travel restrictions imposed until penalties and interest are discharged
